data.narrative:
Adarga is a Series B defense and security software company that has raised $26.2M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 firms—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private—all operating in the same sector and stage.

Two triangulation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis uses total capital raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $50M. Peer-median methodology examines 7 same-sector, same-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $300M to $3.0B—including Dream Security at $3.0B, Harmattan AI at $1.4B, Code Metal at $1.2B, Castelion at $1.0B, and Defense Unicorns at $1.0B—producing a median implied value of $1.0B.

The wide divergence between these methods reflects genuine uncertainty in early-stage defense-tech valuations. The triangulated range spans $42M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $525M. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively to capital deployed; the peer-median reflects sector momentum and comparable exit valuations but carries execution and market risk. Key uncertainties include Adarga's differentiation within the peer cohort, revenue trajectory relative to comparables, and customer concentration. Additional clarity on revenue run-rate, retention, and near-term funding needs would narrow this range substantially.
